Right now Lovable has competition in the vibe coding arena. Like Replit for example. I found Replit to be better in my testing.
I'm using Lovable heavily for PM prototyping and it's great. I think, if anything, current subscription may be too cheap.

As a product designer, I'm seriously looking at using Lovable for quick ideation and prototyping. Showing users Figma screens can be nice, but virtually everybody responds better to an interactive prototype.
Perhaps me just stupid and do prompts bad, but I can't make Lovable come up with anything really differentiated as a design. I'm curious if folks have tips on how to use it well.

According to their blog, Lovable has 30,000+ paying customers but there are 25,000 new apps created per day with 1.2M apps overall - clearly almost all apps are being created by free users, raising unit economics concerns given LLM, hosting, and sandbox costs.
As a programmer this is not good enough yet to warrant my time using it for production code (nor are its competitors). However if I need to prototype for throwaway it would be ok.

One example: the AI that vibe-coded the Supabase backend (Lovable), which uses remote procedure calls, implemented it with flawed access control logic, essentially blocking authenticated users and allowing access to unauthenticated users - affecting 18,000 users.

Lovable is marketed to non developers, so their core users wouldn't understand a security flaw if it flashed red. Non-dev friends built cool apps on Lovable that all look the same with a different color palette, and are now mostly abandoned, waiting for the subscription to expire.
I recently played a little story based game that was hosted on Lovable. It worked reasonably well!
Lovable and bolt took a massive shortcut: they outsourced the backend to a third party (supabase). This makes their ceiling to build 'useful' software incredibly low.
Yes, I use it for something very unusual: Vibe coding a classic Point & Click adventure game, only in German so far and very early in development.
I used Claude Code a lot, but Lovable is the fastest way to get a log-in system and database, so a great option for a true MVP.

My friend built his niche news site with lovable. It built some absolute monstrosity with cloudflare workers - every page view incurred a call to Wordpress, no proper caching, 3+ second TTFB. Lovable would only use their own framework 'Tanstack Start', wouldn't build an AstroJS site. Switched to Cursor and rebuilt with Astro in a couple of days - now blazing fast.

I was on the agent team at Lovable. Lovable is a normal, fully capable agent harness with a Linux box, MCPs, skills, subagents, browser. You can ask it to grab Rust from nixpkgs, write a raytracer, compile to WASM, and it will do it, or write an OS in assembly and run it in v86.
